subject: Damaged library book
situation: You borrowed a book from the university library. Yesterday you spilled coffee on it, and some pages are now stained. The book is due back next week.
bullets: Explain what happened to the book
Ask what you should do now
Offer a way to solve the problem

subject: Part-time job
situation: You saw a sign at the campus café saying that they need part-time workers for the weekend. You are interested in the job.
bullets: Say why you are writing
Describe a skill or experience that makes you a good worker
Ask a question about the job

subject: Missed class
situation: You were sick and missed yesterday's biology class. Your classmate Dana always takes careful notes. There is a quiz on Friday.
bullets: Tell Dana why you missed the class
Ask her for help with the notes
Suggest how you could thank her

subject: Problem in my room
situation: You live in a student residence. The heater in your room stopped working two days ago, and the room is very cold at night.
bullets: Describe the problem
Explain how it is affecting you
Ask when it can be repaired

subject: Joining the swimming team
situation: You want to join the university swimming team, but you missed the first meeting of the semester.
bullets: Explain why you are writing
Describe your experience with swimming
Ask what you need to do next

subject: Your package
situation: A delivery driver left a package for your neighbor, Mrs. Lee, at your door while she was away. You are leaving for a trip tomorrow morning.
bullets: Tell her about the package
Explain why you cannot keep it for long
Suggest a way for her to get it

subject: Request to change my presentation date
situation: You are scheduled to give a presentation in Professor Klein's history class next Tuesday. However, you have just been invited to a job interview at the same time.
bullets: Explain your situation
Request a different presentation date
Suggest how you could make the change easy for the professor

subject: Incorrect charge on my account
situation: You checked your student account online and noticed that you were charged a late fee for housing, even though you paid on time.
bullets: Describe the charge you noticed
Explain why you believe it is a mistake
Ask what you need to do to correct it

subject: Volunteering at the science fair
situation: Your town is holding a science fair for children next month. The coordinator, Mr. Ortiz, is looking for volunteers to help run activities.
bullets: Express your interest in volunteering
Describe how your skills could help
Ask about the schedule or training

subject: Our group project
situation: You are working on a group project with three classmates. One member, Lena, has not replied to messages for a week, and the deadline is in five days.
bullets: Explain why you are worried
Describe what still needs to be done
Propose a plan for finishing the project

subject: Suggestion for Riverside Park
situation: You often go running in Riverside Park in the evening. The path is very dark after sunset, and several runners have nearly fallen.
bullets: Describe the problem
Explain why it matters to park users
Suggest a possible solution

subject: Research assistant position
situation: Dr. Nguyen, a psychology professor, posted an announcement looking for a student research assistant for the summer. You took her course last year and enjoyed it.
bullets: Explain why you are interested in the position
Describe relevant experience or skills
Ask a question about the responsibilities

subject: Faulty headphones
situation: You ordered wireless headphones online. When they arrived, the left side did not work. You have already tried charging them fully.
bullets: Describe the problem with the product
Explain what you have already tried
Say what you would like the company to do

subject: Feedback on my essay
situation: You received a lower grade than you expected on an essay for Professor Adams's sociology course. The comments say that your argument was unclear, but you are not sure what to improve.
bullets: Thank the professor for the comments
Explain which part you do not understand
Ask for a meeting or specific advice

subject: Response to your article on study spaces
situation: The student newspaper published an article claiming that students rarely use the library's quiet study rooms and that the rooms should be turned into a café. You use the rooms regularly and disagree.
bullets: Explain your reaction to the article
Give evidence or examples that challenge its claim
Propose an alternative that could satisfy different students

subject: Workload during exams
situation: You are doing a part-time internship at a marketing company. Your final exams start in two weeks, and your supervisor has just given you a large new assignment due at the same time.
bullets: Show that you value the assignment
Explain the conflict with your exams
Suggest a realistic arrangement

subject: Proposed quiet hours
situation: The residence hall committee is proposing quiet hours from 9 p.m. to 9 a.m. every day. Some residents support the idea, but others, including you, think it is too strict.
bullets: State your opinion of the proposal
Explain how it would affect residents like you
Suggest a compromise

subject: Study abroad credits
situation: You recently returned from a semester abroad. Your university has accepted only two of the four courses you took, even though you received approval before leaving.
bullets: Explain the situation clearly
Refer to the approval you received
Request a specific action and timeline

subject: Guest speaker for our club
situation: You lead the environmental club at your university. Professor Mendes recently published a book on urban ecology, and the club would like to invite her to speak.
bullets: Introduce yourself and the club
Explain why her work interests the members
Describe the event and ask about her availability

subject: Accessibility of the new lecture hall
situation: The university has opened a new lecture hall. A friend of yours who uses a wheelchair has found that the only accessible entrance is often locked in the evening.
bullets: Describe the problem you have observed
Explain its consequences for students
Recommend steps the university could take

subject: Wrong edition of a textbook
situation: You bought a chemistry textbook at the campus bookstore last week. Today your professor told the class that you need the newest edition, but you have an older one. You still have the receipt.
bullets: Explain which book you bought
Say why the book is a problem
Ask how you can exchange it

subject: Joining the swimming club
situation: You want to join the university swimming club, but you have not found any information about it on the website. You can swim, but you are not a very fast swimmer.
bullets: Say why you are writing
Describe your swimming experience
Ask a question about the schedule or the price

subject: Kitchen cleaning
situation: You and your roommate Alex share a small kitchen. Lately, dirty dishes have stayed in the sink for several days, and you want to solve the problem in a friendly way.
bullets: Explain the problem
Suggest a simple plan for cleaning
Ask Alex what he thinks

subject: Absence next Tuesday
situation: You have a dentist appointment next Tuesday at the same time as your history class. The appointment was very hard to get, so you do not want to change it. Next week the class will have a short test.
bullets: Explain why you cannot come
Ask about the test
Say what you can do to catch up

subject: Lost student card
situation: You think you left your student card on the campus bus this morning. The bus was number 4, and you got off near the science building at about 8:30. You need the card to enter the library.
bullets: Describe what you lost and where
Ask if anyone has found it
Give your contact information

subject: English conversation club
situation: You saw a poster for an English conversation club at the Language Center. You would like to practice speaking with other students, but the poster does not say when the club meets.
bullets: Say why you are writing
Describe how well you speak English now
Ask when the club meets

subject: No Wi-Fi in my room
situation: The Wi-Fi in your dormitory room stopped working three days ago. Other students on your floor have internet, and you need it to send your homework before the deadline on Friday.
bullets: Describe the problem
Explain why it is urgent
Ask when someone can help

subject: My birthday dinner
situation: Your birthday is next Saturday, and you are planning a dinner at a small restaurant near campus. You would like Emma, who is one of your best friends, to come.
bullets: Invite Emma to the dinner
Give the time and place
Ask if she needs any special food

subject: Choosing a class
situation: You need to choose one more class for next semester. You are interested in both Introduction to Psychology and Basic Statistics, but you can only take one of them.
bullets: Name the two classes
Explain why you cannot decide
Ask for advice

subject: Vegetarian meals
situation: You are a vegetarian and eat in the university dining hall every day. You have noticed that there is usually only one vegetarian dish, and it is often the same one.
bullets: Explain what you have noticed
Suggest one or two new dishes
Thank her for considering your idea

subject: Letter of recommendation
situation: You are applying for a summer exchange program, and the application requires a letter of recommendation from a professor. You took Professor Hall's course last year and received a high grade. The deadline is in three weeks.
bullets: Ask Professor Hall for a letter
Remind him why he knows your work well
Offer information that will make the task easier

subject: Missing scholarship document
situation: You received a message from the Financial Aid Office saying that a document is missing from your scholarship file. You submitted all the required papers last month and kept a copy of the confirmation. The scholarship payment is due soon.
bullets: Explain why you are surprised by the message
Describe what you did to submit your documents
Ask what should happen next

subject: Request to change rooms
situation: Your dormitory room is next to a lounge where students often talk and play music until after midnight. You have asked them to be quiet several times, but nothing has changed, and you are having trouble studying for exams.
bullets: Explain the situation
Describe how it affects you
Request a solution

subject: Joining your research project
situation: Dr. Ibrahim gave a talk about her research on local bird populations. You found it fascinating and would like to get involved as a volunteer, although you have no laboratory experience.
bullets: Express your interest in the project
Explain what you can contribute
Ask about the next step

subject: A late-night study space
situation: The main library closes at 10 p.m., but many students study much later, especially before exams. Some of them have to go back to noisy dormitories or to expensive cafés, and you think the university should offer a better option.
bullets: Describe the problem
Propose a solution
Explain how it would benefit students

subject: Help with interview preparation
situation: You have been invited to a job interview at a local company for a summer position. This is your first formal interview, and you feel nervous. The Career Center offers practice sessions, but the schedule is full this week.
bullets: Explain your situation
Say what kind of help you need
Suggest when you could meet

subject: Rescheduling our meeting
situation: Your group is preparing a presentation for next Monday. You planned to meet on Thursday, but your work shift has just been changed and you cannot come. Jordan is the group leader and has been organizing the project.
bullets: Apologize for the change
Propose a new time or another way to meet
Offer to complete some extra work

subject: Student open mic night
situation: There is a small café near campus where students often study. You belong to the university music club and think the café would be a good place for a monthly open mic night, when students could perform songs and read poems.
bullets: Introduce your idea
Explain why it would be good for the café
Ask to arrange a meeting

subject: Question about my quiz grade
situation: You received a grade of 6 out of 10 on a quiz, but you think one of your answers was correct. You have compared your answer with the textbook and with your lecture notes, and you believe the question was a little unclear.
bullets: Politely explain your concern
Support your opinion with evidence
Ask whether the grade could be reviewed

subject: Sending my transcript
situation: You need to send an official transcript to a university in another country. The application deadline is in ten days, and you have heard that the Registrar's Office sometimes takes a long time to process requests.
bullets: State what you need
Explain why the timing matters
Ask about the fastest way to send it

subject: Extension for my report
situation: You were chosen to represent your university at a student conference next week. Because of the travel and meetings, you will not be able to finish the lab report for Dr. Levine's course by Friday, although you have already collected all the data.
bullets: Explain the situation
Request more time
Suggest a new deadline

subject: Construction noise near the lecture hall
situation: For the past two weeks, building work outside Lecture Hall B has been so loud that students cannot hear the professors. Several classes have been interrupted, and your class has an important lecture next Wednesday.
bullets: Describe the problem
Explain how it affects your class
Suggest a possible solution

subject: Extended library hours during exams
situation: The university library currently closes at 10 p.m. even during final exams. Many students, including those who work during the day, find it difficult to study in their dormitories. You have spoken with classmates and believe that the dean could improve the situation at a reasonable cost.
bullets: Present the problem clearly
Offer a realistic proposal
Anticipate and answer a possible objection

subject: Alternative to the final paper
situation: Your course in design history requires a final paper of 3,000 words. You have been working on a related project, a small exhibition of student posters, and you believe it demonstrates the same learning outcomes more effectively than a traditional paper.
bullets: Explain your request
Show how the project meets the course goals
Propose a way to evaluate it fairly

subject: The new recycling policy
situation: The university has replaced all separate recycling bins with a single large container in each building. The office says this will increase participation, but you have noticed that people now throw almost everything into it, including food waste.
bullets: Express your concern
Explain why the policy may not achieve its goal
Recommend an alternative

subject: Regarding the placement offer
situation: You were offered an internship at a large firm, but you have since been invited to join a research project in your department, which is more relevant to your future studies. You do not want to damage your relationship with the internship program.
bullets: Thank him for the offer
Explain your decision tactfully
Propose a way to stay in contact

subject: Correction request
situation: Last week the university newspaper published an article about student clubs. It stated that the Chess Club has only five members and meets irregularly. In fact, the club has more than forty members and meets twice a week. As the club's secretary, you want this corrected.
bullets: Identify the mistake precisely
Explain why accuracy matters to the club
Request a specific correction

subject: Changes to my research method
situation: Dr. Kaplan approved your thesis proposal, which relied on a large survey. After starting the project, you found that few people respond to the survey, so you want to switch to a smaller number of in-depth interviews.
bullets: Explain what you have discovered
Justify the new approach
Ask for feedback or approval

subject: Clarity of the room assignment process
situation: You and three friends applied together for a four-person apartment but were placed in separate buildings. The housing website says that group requests are given priority, yet no one has explained how the decision was made.
bullets: State your concern respectfully
Request an explanation of the process
Propose a constructive way to resolve the situation

subject: Scheduling conflict with a guest seminar
situation: A well-known economist will give a guest seminar next Thursday, but it overlaps with Professor Brandt's tutorial. Attending the seminar would help your thesis, and the tutorial that day covers material you already know well.
bullets: Explain the conflict
Justify why attending the seminar is valuable
Offer a plan to make up the missed tutorial

subject: Request for a recommendation letter deadline
situation: You are applying for a competitive summer research program, and the application deadline is in ten days. Professor Lindqvist supervised your last project but has not yet agreed to write a recommendation letter, and you are worried that there will not be enough time.
bullets: Explain your situation and the deadline
Provide information that will make the letter easier to write
Propose a way to handle the timing if he is very busy

subject: Disability accommodation for exams
situation: You have a temporary hand injury and cannot write quickly for long periods. Your midterm exams begin in two weeks, and the exam rules do not mention extra time or a laptop. You would like to know whether an adjustment is possible.
bullets: Describe your circumstances
Request a specific adjustment
Offer to provide supporting documentation

subject: Concerns about a course being cancelled
situation: The department has announced that an advanced elective you planned to take next semester will be cancelled because too few students enrolled. The course is required for your intended specialization, and you know several other students who are also affected.
bullets: Express your concern about the cancellation
Explain how it affects you and others
Suggest an alternative that would solve the problem

subject: Proposal for a charity run
situation: Your student club would like to organize a charity run on campus in the spring to raise money for a local food bank. You expect about two hundred participants and need permission to use the main paths and the sports field for one morning.
bullets: Introduce the event and its purpose
Describe what you need from the campus
Offer to meet to discuss safety arrangements

subject: Disagreement about a group-work grade
situation: Your group received a single grade for a joint report, but you did most of the writing while two teammates contributed very little. You do not want to accuse anyone unfairly, yet you believe the grade should reflect each person's contribution.
bullets: Explain your concern respectfully
Support it with specific details
Suggest how the grading could be made fairer

subject: Peer-tutoring program for international students
situation: You have noticed that new international students often struggle in their first semester because they are unfamiliar with academic writing conventions. You think a peer-tutoring program run by senior students could help, and you would like to help set it up.
bullets: Describe the problem you have observed
Present your idea for a solution
Explain what role you could play
